lessons.title: Listen and speak: introducing myself and a friend
lessons.objective: Introduce oneself (name, age, class) and introduce a friend.
lessons.course:
To introduce myself, I say: My name is Ayuk. I am six years old. I am in Class 1.
To introduce a friend, I say: This is my friend. Her name is Manka. or His name is Neba.

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
My name is …
I am … years old.
This is my friend. His name is …

lessons.model: On the first day of school, Manka stands up and says: “Good morning. My name is Manka. I am six years old.” Then she shows her friend: “This is my friend. His name is Neba.”
lessons.guided: Play “new pupil”: say your name and age, then introduce a toy or a family member as your friend.
lessons.answer: For example: My name is Ayuk. I am six years old.
lessons.remediation: Say only “My name is …” several times, then add the age.
lessons.transfer: Introduce a member of your family to a visitor.
lessons.materials: A doll or a puppet to play the friend.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
practice.explanation: A sentence starts with a capital letter.

practice.prompt: Complete: This is my friend. ___ name is Manka (a girl).
practice.explanation: For a girl we say her; for a boy we say his.

practice.prompt: Listen and say after the voice.
practice.listen: My name is Ashu. I am six years old. I am in Class 1.
practice.answer: My name is Ashu. I am six years old. I am in Class 1.
practice.explanation: Speak slowly and look at the person.

lessons.title: Read: simple words and short sentences
lessons.objective: Read simple words and short sentences aloud, from left to right, holding the book correctly.
lessons.course:
We hold the book the right way up and turn pages from right to left. We read each line from left to right and from top to bottom.
Short sentences: I sit. I can read. The pen is red.

support.title: Read with the adult
support.text:
I sit.
I can read.
The pen is red.

lessons.model: The adult shows how to hold a book, puts a finger under the first word and reads: “I… can… read.”
lessons.guided: Read each sentence with a finger under the words. Then read it again without the finger.
lessons.exercise: Read the sentence: The pen is red.
lessons.remediation: Read the sentence word by word with the adult, then read it again together.
lessons.transfer: Read the name of your school or your class on a sign.
lessons.materials: A short school reader or sentence cards.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
practice.explanation: We read from left to right.

practice.prompt: Where do we start to read a line?
practice.explanation: We read from left to right.

practice.prompt: Read and answer: “The bag is red.” What colour is the bag?
practice.explanation: The sentence says the bag is red.

lessons.title: Write: copying names
lessons.objective: Copy one’s own name and the names of classmates correctly, with a capital letter.
lessons.course: A person’s name starts with a capital letter: Ayuk, Bih, Neba. We copy each letter in order, from left to right, and leave a space between two names.
lessons.model: The adult writes three names on cards and copies one slowly: “A… y… u… k: Ayuk.”
lessons.guided: Choose two name cards. Copy each name under the model. Check letter by letter.
lessons.remediation: Copy one letter, check it, then copy the next.
lessons.transfer: Write the names of two people in your family.

practice.prompt: Copy the names: Bih and Tabi.
practice.answer: Bih and Tabi, each with a capital letter.
practice.explanation: Names start with a capital letter.

practice.prompt: Which name is written correctly?
practice.explanation: Only the first letter of a name is a capital.

practice.prompt: Put the letters in order to write the name “Bih”.
practice.explanation: Copy the letters in order.

lessons.title: I, you, he, she, we, they
lessons.objective: Use personal pronouns to talk about oneself and others.
lessons.course:
Pronouns replace names. I is me. You is the person I talk to. He is a boy or a man. She is a girl or a woman. We is me and others. They is other people.
Neba is in class → He is in class. Bih and Manka sing → They sing.

support.title: Say with the adult
support.text:
I  you  he  she  we  they
Bih is happy. → She is happy.

lessons.model: The adult points: “I am the teacher. You are a pupil. He is Neba. She is Bih. We are in Class 1. They are in Class 2.”
lessons.guided: Point to people (or dolls) and say the right pronoun. Then replace a name in a sentence with he, she or they.
lessons.exercise: Replace the name: Ayuk is tall. → ___ is tall.
lessons.remediation: Practise he and she only, with pictures of a boy and a girl.
lessons.transfer: Talk about your family with he and she: “She is my mother.”
lessons.materials: Pictures of a boy, a girl, a group of children.

practice.prompt: Complete with he, she or they.
practice.text: Bih reads. [[She]] reads. Tabi and Ekane play. [[They]] play.
practice.explanation: She for a girl, they for more than one person.

practice.prompt: Match each name with the pronoun.
practice.answer: Neba: he; Manka: she; Neba and Manka: they.
practice.explanation: The pronoun replaces the name.

practice.prompt: Which pronoun do you use for yourself?
practice.explanation: I is used to talk about oneself.

lessons.title: The days of the week
lessons.objective: Name the days of the week in order and relate each day to an event.
lessons.course:
A week has 7 days: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.
We go to school from Monday to Friday. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.
lessons.model: The adult shows a calendar: “Today is Wednesday. Yesterday was Tuesday. Tomorrow will be Thursday.”
lessons.guided: Say the days in order with a song or a clap. Put a card on each day: school days and weekend days.
lessons.remediation: Learn the school days first, Monday to Friday.
lessons.transfer: Say what you do on Sunday with your family.

practice.prompt: Put the days in order.
practice.explanation: These are the school days.

practice.prompt: How many days are there in a week?
practice.explanation: Monday to Sunday: 7 days.

practice.prompt: Which day is in the weekend?
practice.explanation: Saturday and Sunday make the weekend.

lessons.title: Tens and units up to 50
lessons.objective: Place numbers up to 50 under tens (T) and units (U).
lessons.course:
In 34 there are 3 tens and 4 units. We write it in a table: T | U → 3 | 4.
Ten units make one ten.
lessons.model: The adult bundles 30 sticks into 3 bundles of ten and adds 4 loose sticks: “3 tens and 4 units: 34.”
lessons.guided: Make numbers with bundles and loose sticks. Write each one in a T | U table.
lessons.exercise: How many tens are there in 47?
lessons.remediation: Work up to 20 first: 1 ten and some units.
lessons.transfer: Count the pupils of your class in tens and units.
lessons.materials: Sticks, rubber bands, a T | U table.

practice.prompt: 2 tens and 5 units. Which number?
Complete the table for 38.
Which number has 5 tens and 0 units?
practice.explanation: 5 tens = 50.

lessons.title: Taking away within 20
lessons.objective: Subtract within 20 using objects and the signs − and =.
lessons.course:
To take away is to remove some. 9 pencils, 3 are given away: 6 are left.
We write: 9 − 3 = 6. The sign − means “take away”.
lessons.model: The adult puts 10 pieces of chalk on the table and gives away 4: “10 take away 4 leaves 6. 10 − 4 = 6.”
lessons.guided: Make a group, take some away and count what is left. Write the subtraction.
lessons.exercise: There are 15 pupils. 5 go home. How many are left?
lessons.transfer: Count the mangoes in a bowl before and after a snack.

practice.explanation: Count back 2 from 12: 11, 10.

practice.prompt: Complete the subtractions.
practice.explanation: Take away, then count what is left.

practice.prompt: What does the sign − mean?
practice.explanation: − means we take away.

lessons.title: Counting with tallies in 2s
lessons.objective: Collect simple data and count by tallying in twos.
lessons.course:
To count quickly, we make tally marks: | for each thing. We can count tallies in 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.
We use tallies to count things at school: boys, girls, books.
lessons.model: The adult counts the pairs of shoes at the door in 2s: “2, 4, 6, 8. Eight shoes.”
lessons.guided: Count your classmates’ eyes or hands in 2s. Make tally marks in pairs and count them.
lessons.remediation: Count objects in pairs: put them two by two, then count.
lessons.transfer: Count the pairs of socks at home in 2s.
lessons.materials: Pairs of shoes or socks, chalk.

practice.prompt: How many hands do 4 children have? Count in 2s.
Complete the count in 2s.
practice.explanation: Add 2 each time.

practice.prompt: Put the numbers in the order of counting in 2s.
practice.explanation: Each time we add 2.

lessons.title: Using the toilet and washing my hands
lessons.objective: Locate the school toilet, use it properly and wash hands with soap after using it.
lessons.course:
At school we use the toilet, not the bush. We keep the toilet clean and we flush or cover after use.
After the toilet, we always wash our hands with soap and clean water: wet, soap, rub, rinse, dry.
lessons.model: During break, Ayuk goes to the school toilet. Then he goes to the tap, wets his hands, rubs them with soap, rinses and dries them.
lessons.guided: Visit the school toilet with the teacher. Then practise the five steps of hand washing at the tap.
lessons.exercise: What do we do after using the toilet?
lessons.answer: We wash our hands with soap and water.
accept: We wash our hands with soap and water
lessons.remediation: Practise the five steps with gestures and a song.
lessons.transfer: At home, remind your brothers and sisters to wash their hands after the toilet.
lessons.materials: Soap, clean water, a bowl, a towel.

practice.prompt: Put the steps of hand washing in order.
practice.explanation: Follow the five steps each time.

practice.prompt: Where do we go to ease ourselves at school?
practice.explanation: We always use the toilet and keep it clean.

practice.prompt: With what do we wash our hands?
practice.explanation: Soap removes the dirt and germs.

lessons.title: Les voyelles a, e, i, o, u
lessons.objective: Reconnaître et lire les voyelles a, e, i, o, u en français.
lessons.course:
En français, les voyelles sont : a, e, i, o, u.
a comme dans « ami », e comme dans « le », i comme dans « île », o comme dans « olive », u comme dans « une ».
Attention : en français, u ne se dit pas comme en anglais ; on avance les lèvres.

support.title: Lis avec l’adulte
support.text:
a  e  i  o  u
ami  le  île  olive  une

lessons.model: L’adulte montre la lettre o et dit : « o, comme dans olive. » Puis il montre u et avance les lèvres : « u, comme dans une. »
lessons.guided: Cherche les voyelles dans des étiquettes de mots. Entoure-les et dis leur son.
lessons.exercise: Quelle voyelle entends-tu au début de « ami » ?
lessons.remediation: Travaille deux voyelles par jour avec un geste pour chacune.
lessons.transfer: Cherche la lettre a dans ton prénom ou dans le nom de ta rue.
lessons.materials: Étiquettes de lettres et de mots.

practice.prompt: Remets les voyelles dans l’ordre.
practice.explanation: C’est l’ordre de l’alphabet.

practice.prompt: Quelle lettre est une voyelle ?
practice.explanation: o est une voyelle ; m et t sont des consonnes.

practice.prompt: Écoute et répète les voyelles.
practice.explanation: Ouvre bien la bouche.

lessons.title: Our class rules
lessons.objective: Discuss school rules and apply them in class and in the yard.
lessons.course:
At school we follow rules: come on time, wear the uniform, raise your hand to speak, listen to the teacher, keep the classroom clean, play without fighting.
When we break a rule, we say sorry and do better.
lessons.model: Manka wants to answer. She raises her hand and waits. The teacher says: “Yes, Manka.”
lessons.guided: With the class or the family, write three class rules. Mime each rule.
lessons.exercise: What do you do when you want to speak in class?
lessons.remediation: Practise one rule at a time with a game (raise your hand before speaking).
lessons.transfer: Tell an adult one school rule you followed today.
lessons.materials: A big sheet of paper for the class rules.

practice.prompt: Which one is a school rule?
practice.explanation: We come to school on time.

practice.prompt: Put in order: what Ayuk does when he arrives late.
practice.answer: knocks, says sorry, sits down quietly.
practice.explanation: We say sorry when we break a rule.

practice.prompt: Where do we put papers we do not need?
practice.explanation: We keep the classroom clean.

lessons.title: Threading beads for a school necklace
lessons.objective: Thread beads or seeds to make a pattern.
lessons.course:
Threading means passing a string through holes. We can thread beads, seeds, bottle tops with holes or pieces of straw.
We can make a pattern: red, blue, red, blue…
lessons.model: Manka threads beads on a string: red, yellow, red, yellow. She makes a necklace to wear on Culture Day.
lessons.guided: Thread beads or straw pieces on a string with a pattern. Say the pattern aloud.
lessons.exercise: Continue the pattern: red, blue, red, blue, …
lessons.remediation: Thread big pieces (pieces of straw) before small beads.
lessons.transfer: Make a bracelet for a friend.
lessons.materials: String, beads, seeds with holes or pieces of straw.

practice.prompt: Put the beads in the order of the pattern.
practice.explanation: The pattern repeats.

practice.prompt: What do we pass through the holes of the beads?
practice.explanation: Threading uses a string.

practice.prompt: How many beads are there in “red, yellow, red, yellow, red”?
practice.explanation: Count each bead: 5.

lessons.title: A school song
lessons.objective: Sing a short song with the right rhythm and enjoy singing with others.
lessons.course: Singing together is a joy. We listen to the song, we learn it line by line, we sing with a clear voice and we keep the rhythm by clapping.

support.title: Klassia school song
support.text:
Good morning, school, good morning, friends,
we learn, we play, we read and write,
we help each other, hand in hand,
good morning, school, the day is bright!

lessons.model: The adult sings the song slowly and claps on each line. The children repeat each line.
lessons.guided: Learn the song line by line. Then sing it all together while clapping.
lessons.exercise: What do we do with our hands to keep the rhythm?
lessons.remediation: Sing the first line only, several times, then add the second.
lessons.transfer: Sing the song at home for your family.

practice.prompt: Listen to the song and sing it after the voice.
practice.listen: Good morning, school, good morning, friends, we learn, we play, we read and write, we help each other, hand in hand, good morning, school, the day is bright!
practice.answer: The song sung line by line.
practice.explanation: Sing with a clear voice.

practice.prompt: Put the lines of the song in order.
items: Good morning, school, good morning, friends,
we learn, we play, we read and write,
we help each other, hand in hand,
good morning, school, the day is bright!
practice.explanation: The song starts and ends with “good morning, school”.

practice.prompt: Which word rhymes with “write”?
practice.explanation: write – bright: they end with the same sound.

lessons.title: Relay race: touch and run
lessons.objective: Take part in a relay, stay attentive and help the team.
lessons.course:
In a relay, the team is in a line. The first runner runs to a mark and comes back, touches the hand of the next runner, who then runs. The team that finishes first wins.
We stay attentive and we encourage our team.
lessons.model: Two teams line up. The adult says “Go!” The first runners run, come back and touch the next hands.
lessons.guided: Play a relay in two teams. Practise touching the hand at the right moment.
lessons.exercise: When does the next runner start?
lessons.remediation: Walk the relay first, then run.
lessons.transfer: Organise a small relay with friends in the yard.

practice.prompt: Put the relay in order.
items: The first runner runs to the mark.
He touches the next runner’s hand.
practice.answer: run, come back, touch, next runner starts.
practice.explanation: The touch passes the turn.

practice.prompt: What helps a team win a relay?
practice.explanation: Good team members pay attention.

practice.prompt: There are 4 runners in a team. How many touches are needed?
practice.explanation: Runner 1 touches 2, 2 touches 3, 3 touches 4: 3 touches.

lessons.title: Introducing myself in our language
lessons.objective: Introduce oneself and others in the home language.
lessons.course: In our language too, we can say our name and the name of a friend. We look at the person, speak clearly and smile.
lessons.model: The adult says in the family language: “My name is …”, then the child repeats with his own name.
lessons.guided: Ask the adult how to say “My name is …” and “This is my friend …” in the family language. Practise.
lessons.exercise: Introduce yourself in your family language.
lessons.answer: The child says his name in the family language.
lessons.remediation: Say only your name with the help of the adult.
lessons.transfer: Introduce yourself in the family language to a grandparent or an elder.

practice.prompt: Say “This is my friend …” in your family language.
practice.answer: The sentence in the family language.
practice.explanation: Ask an adult to help you.

practice.prompt: How do we introduce ourselves well?
choices: look at the person and speak clearly
look at the floor and whisper
practice.answer: look at the person and speak clearly
practice.explanation: Clear speech shows respect.

practice.prompt: Say your name and your age in English.
practice.answer: My name is … I am … years old.
practice.explanation: You can also say it in your family language.

lessons.title: The parts of a computer
lessons.objective: Identify the main parts of a computer: monitor, keyboard, mouse and system unit.
lessons.course:
A computer has main parts. The monitor (screen) shows pictures and words. The keyboard has keys to type letters and numbers. The mouse moves the arrow on the screen. The system unit is the box that makes the computer work.
Sometimes a printer prints on paper.
lessons.model: In the school office, the head teacher types on the keyboard and the words appear on the monitor.
lessons.guided: Look at a computer or a picture. Point to each part and say its name.
lessons.exercise: Which part shows pictures and words?
lessons.remediation: Learn two parts first: the screen and the keyboard.
lessons.transfer: Draw a computer and write the names of its parts with an adult.
lessons.materials: A computer or a picture of one.

practice.prompt: Match each part with what it does.
practice.answer: monitor: shows; keyboard: types; mouse: moves the arrow.
practice.explanation: Each part has its job.

practice.prompt: Which part prints on paper?
practice.explanation: The printer puts words and pictures on paper.

practice.prompt: Draw a computer with its four main parts.
practice.answer: A drawing with monitor, keyboard, mouse and system unit.
practice.explanation: Name each part.
